confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly reports random assignment to the assistance conditions: "Triads were randomly assigned to human-only teams or to groups that included one or two AI agents programmed with distinct personas, supportive or contrarian."
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Introduction, paragraph beginning "In this mixed-design study".

confirmed.statement: S1 also explicitly reports random formation of three-member groups; each participant completes one task domain, with six team/persona conditions within each of three tasks.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, section 3.2; p. 6, Figure 2 caption and section 3.3.

confirmed.statement: AI teammates participate in the discussion of participants' own tasks, including generating and refining an original movie plot; the manipulation is assistance during creative work, not merely whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 3.2, Procedure; p. 7, section 3.3, Creative ideation task; p. 28, Appendix A.3.

confirmed.statement: The paper frames the agents as generative conversational AI and supplies the system prompts that generate their supportive or contrarian responses; the specific model, provider, version, and model-sampling settings are not identified.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, abstract and keywords (Generative AI; Large language model); pp. 7-8, sections 3.4-3.5; pp. 29-31, Appendix B. Full document checked for a model identifier.

confirmed.statement: The arm definitions match: H3 has three humans; H2_C/H2_S have two humans and one contrarian/supportive AI; H1_C/H1_S have one human and two contrarian/supportive AIs; H1_M has one human and one AI of each persona.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-6, section 3.2 and Table 2; p. 39, Table 16 note defining all condition codes.

confirmed.statement: H3 provides two human partners to each participant and no AI, supporting the form's active human-partner comparator coding; comparisons between AI personas or compositions change the AI configuration.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, section 3.2, Experimental conditions; p. 39, Table 16 condition key; creativity-codebook.md, section 5, Comparison type.

confirmed.statement: AI involvement is undisclosed during the task, and agents contribute under persona prompts with probabilistic scheduling and turn-taking limits, matching the coded AI-teammate role.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, section 3.2, Procedure and Identity masking; pp. 7-8, sections 3.4-3.5; pp. 29-31, Appendix B.

confirmed.statement: S1 has a fixed individual baseline, group discussion, and individual post-task sequence. The assistance conditions differ between teams; repeated assessment does not constitute a crossover between AI conditions, so randomized condition order is inapplicable.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 4-5, section 3.2; p. 6, Figure 2 caption; creativity-codebook.md, section 3, criterion 1.

confirmed.statement: All 18 analyzed arm counts in the form match Table 2 and sum to the stated analytic sample; a separate allocation-stage breakdown and an allocation algorithm are not reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 3-4, section 3.1; pp. 4-6, section 3.2 and Table 2. All Table 2 cells checked directly in PDF text.

confirmed.statement: S2 is an independent pilot in which every participant interacts with two AI teammates under the selected protocol; no randomized condition contrast is reported, consistent with its not_stated assignment coding.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, section 3.5, independent pilot paragraph.

summary: The PDF explicitly reports random assignment of triads to human-only or generative-AI teammate conditions during participants' own creative work. The coded arms, AI role, and mixed pre/post design are supported, so criterion 1 holds.
